item.title: Asahiyama Zoo — Guide
item.description: Asahiyama Zoo, in Asahikawa in central Hokkaido, is one of Japan’s most famous and popular zoos, celebrated for its pioneering approach to displaying animals. Rather than static enclosures, it uses clever ‘behavioural exhibition’ designs that let visitors see animals moving and behaving naturally, up close and from surprising angles. Highlights include a polar bear enclosure with a domed viewing capsule, a penguin habitat with an underwater tunnel, a seal tank with a vertical clear cylinder the seals shoot through, and enclosures for red pandas, big cats, orangutans and more.

item.title: Asahikawa Winter Festival Guide: Snow Sculptures & Zoo
item.description: Hokkaido’s second city, Asahikawa, is one of Japan’s coldest places — and it embraces winter wholeheartedly. Each February, the Asahikawa Winter Festival raises some of the largest snow sculptures in Japan (it has held world records), with huge snow stages, slides and illuminations along the Ishikari River and downtown. The city is also home to the wildly popular Asahiyama Zoo, famous for its winter penguin walk, and is a hub for Asahikawa-style soy ramen and a gateway to the Daisetsuzan mountains.
